# Design

## Snapshot format

```text
# arch-linter-net public API snapshot — generated by 'arch-linter-net public-api capture'.
# Review changes to this file like any other reviewed artifact.
@format arch-linter-net/public-api-snapshot
@version 1
@contract core-public-api
@assembly ArchLinterNet.Core
class ArchLinterNet.Core.Foo
ctor ArchLinterNet.Core.Foo()
@assembly ArchLinterNet.Cli
class ArchLinterNet.Cli.Bar
```

Determinism rules:

- assemblies ordered ordinal, signatures ordered ordinal within an assembly, duplicates collapsed;
- LF line endings and a trailing newline regardless of host platform;
- no timestamps, paths, machine names, user names, or version stamps — capturing twice from the same assemblies is byte-identical;
- `#` comment lines are informational and are regenerated, not preserved (the file is a generated artifact, unlike a policy).

Bounds (rejected at parse time with a deterministic message):

- at most 200000 entry lines;
- at most 4000 characters per line;
- an entry line before any `@assembly` directive is an error;
- an unknown `@` directive is an error (forward-incompatible files fail loudly instead of silently losing data);
- `@version` other than `1` is an error naming the supported version.

## Path safety

`api_snapshot` is resolved relative to the repository root, must be relative, must not contain a rooted segment or escape the repository root after normalization, and must exist. All four conditions are policy-load-time errors. The same rules apply to `--snapshot`/`--output` paths passed to the CLI, which additionally must not collide with the policy file itself.

## Delta identity

A full normalized signature (`method MyApp.Foo.Bar(System.Int32): System.Void`) changes whenever a parameter or return type changes, so raw set difference reports a re-signed member as an unrelated removal plus addition. Deltas are therefore correlated by an *identity key*:

```text
<kind> <qualified-name-with-arity>/<parameter-count>
```

- parameter count is `-1` when the signature has no parameter list (types, fields, properties without indexers, events);
- top-level commas inside the parameter list are counted at bracket depth 0, so `Dictionary`2[System.String,System.Int32]` counts as one parameter.

Correlation is then: exact-signature matches are paired first; within an identity group the remaining old and new entries are paired positionally in ordinal order and reported as `changed`; any surplus is `removed` or `added`. This is deterministic, order-independent, and never invents a pairing across different member names or arities.

## Where the code lives

The self-architecture policy forbids `Core.Validation` from reaching `Core.Scanning` and forbids `Core.Contracts` from depending on `Core.Execution`. That fixes the layout:

- pure records → `Core.Model`;
- format, differ, and load-time resolver → `Core.Contracts` (which already owns policy loading and has `IArchitectureFileSystem`);
- surface capture (needs the reflection scanner) → `Core.Execution`, exposed on `ArchitectureAnalysisSession`;
- application seam (`Capture`/`Diff`/`Update`/`Migrate`) → `Core.Validation`, mirroring `ArchitectureBaselineApplicationService`;
- file writing stays in the CLI, mirroring `baseline generate` — Core returns content, the host writes it.

## Inline declarations

An inline `declared_api` list stays fully supported and is unioned with any resolved snapshot entries. `public-api update` against a policy whose contract has no `api_snapshot` refuses the write and explains that a safe comment-preserving YAML round-trip is unavailable, pointing at `public-api migrate`. `migrate` writes a snapshot file and reports every inline entry not present in the live surface (`stale`) and every live entry not inline (`undeclared`); with drift present it refuses to write unless `--accept-drift` is passed, so a migration can never silently bless surface that was never reviewed.

## Exact mode and inline lists

Removals need the declared side to be attributable. Snapshot entries carry their assembly; inline `declared_api` entries do not. Exact mode therefore compares the union of the contract's assemblies' actual surface against the union of the declared surface, attributing a removal to the snapshot's assembly when known and to the empty assembly otherwise. This keeps exact mode usable with inline lists without inventing attribution the policy never stated.
